findings.quote: The three tests that sampled the undisturbed environment in the ISS showed very low levels of airborne particulates, averaging fewer than 0.005 mg/m3 from the DustTrak® and fewer than 15 particles/cm3 from the P-Trak® (these are typical readings at the baseline).
findings.about: Undisturbed ISS cabin air: DustTrak readings averaged fewer than 0.005 mg/m3
findings.note: ISS cabin air, Increment 10 (February and March 2005). An upper bound, not a mean.

findings.quote: The three tests that sampled the undisturbed environment in the ISS showed very low levels of airborne particulates, averaging fewer than 0.005 mg/m3 from the DustTrak® and fewer than 15 particles/cm3 from the P-Trak® (these are typical readings at the baseline).
findings.about: Undisturbed ISS cabin air: P-Trak readings averaged fewer than 15 particles/cm3
findings.note: ISS cabin air, Increment 10 (February and March 2005). An upper bound, not a mean.

findings.quote: Overall, the readings from these instruments are almost an order of magnitude below those that would normally be seen in a typical laboratory environment (~ 4,000 – 6,000 pt/cc for P-Trak), but were not totally unexpected, due to the presence of a HEPA filter on the ISS air handling system.
findings.about: Test point #1 readings about an order of magnitude below a typical laboratory (4,000 to 6,000 pt/cc)
findings.note: ISS cabin air, Increment 10 (February and March 2005).

findings.quote: Test point #1 data (Figures 1 and 2) shows that the overall particulate levels in the US Lab atmosphere are very low, about a factor of ten leaner than normal US office conditions.
findings.about: Particle levels in the US Lab about ten times leaner than an office
findings.note: ISS cabin air, Increment 10 (February and March 2005).

findings.quote: Test points #3 and #4 were not appreciably different from Test point #1 for either device.
findings.about: Test points #3 and #4 read like test point #1
findings.note: ISS cabin air, Increment 10 (February and March 2005).

findings.quote: DAFT-1 and -2 showed that the units were ‘apparently working’ and that the air aboard the ISS is almost unbelievably clean. The readings from the devices during that part of the overall experiment though, never crossed the 20% of the operational range threshold, leaving the results somewhat suspect.
findings.about: Increment 10 readings stayed under 20% of the instruments' range
findings.note: ISS cabin air, Increment 10 (February and March 2005).
